sections.partTitle: 听力部分（共两节，满分30分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共5小题；每小题1.5分，满分7.5分）听下面5段对话。每段对话后有一个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。

questions.stem: What is the man doing?
questions.transcript:
【原文】M: Excuse me, I got lost. I took a bus to city hall, but I can't find the place.
W: This is the concert hall, not city hall. To go there, you should take the bus at Grand Hotel over there.

questions.stem: What dress size does the woman want?
questions.transcript:
【原文】M: Can I help you?
W: I'm looking for a size twelve dress.
M: Oh, let me see. An eight, a ten. Ah, you're lucky. I have the prettiest dress here in a twelve. Why don't you try it on?

questions.stem: What is the woman likely to do?
questions.transcript:
【原文】W: Do you think you can take care of everything in the office today?
M: No problem. Just go home and take a rest. If there is anything I feel I cannot handle, I'll call you.

questions.stem: Which tour does the man seem to be interested in?
questions.transcript:
【原文】W: We have a half-day tour, a full-day tour and an evening tour. Which one would you like?
M: What is the schedule of the half-day tour?
W: It sets out at 8:30 a.m. and returns at 2:00 p.m.

questions.stem: Where are the speakers?
questions.transcript:
【原文】M: Now, what seems to be the trouble, Mrs. Stevens?
W: I've been very dizzy lately. And last night, I had some chest pain.
M: Don't worry. Let me have a look.

questions.stem: What does the woman think of the match?
questions.transcript:
【原文】W: Wow. That was a great match. I really like watching tennis games.
M: Me too. I think tennis is an exciting sport.
W: I think so. Do you play tennis, John?
M: Yes, but not very well. Do you play?
W: A little. How about a game on Tuesday afternoon?
M: Sure.

questions.stem: What do the speakers plan to do on Tuesday afternoon?
questions.transcript:
【原文】同第6题对话。W: A little. How about a game on Tuesday afternoon?
M: Sure.

questions.stem: What does the man advise Mrs. White to do?
questions.transcript:
【原文】M: Mrs. White, I'm afraid we have to put you on a strict diet. From now on, you're going to have to stay away from salty food.
W: Does that mean I can't have any more fast food?
M: Right. You can't have any fried food or steaks.
W: What about breakfast food like eggs and sausages?
M: Those are all bad for you. But you can have porridge, bread and orange juice.
W: Well, what about lunch and dinner?
M: Have a salad for lunch. As for dinner, you can have all the vegetables you want. Fish and chicken are also okay.
W: What about dessert? Can I still have ice cream?
M: Yes, but not too much.

questions.stem: Which can be included in Mrs. White's breakfast?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第8题对话。M: Those are all bad for you. But you can have porridge, bread and orange juice.

questions.stem: What is the man?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第8题对话。M: Mrs. White, I'm afraid we have to put you on a strict diet.

questions.stem: How does Nancy look to Daniel?
questions.transcript:
【原文】M: Hi Nancy! You look worried. What's wrong?
W: Well Daniel, have you ever felt nervous on stage?
M: Sure. Do you remember that play I was in a few years ago? I knew my lines, but I was terrified to have to recite them in front of an audience. As soon as I saw the crowd of people down there, my heart beat so fast that I was unable to say a single word.
W: That's how I feel just thinking about the spelling competition next week.
M: I didn't know you made it to the finals.
W: I'm worried I'll get nervous and freeze on stage. I might forget how to spell everything, even my own name. I don't know what to do.
M: Nancy, I know that you're not going to forget how to spell your name. I'll help you get through this. I'll go to the school hall with you to practice. Then I'll teach you an exercise my baseball coach taught me. Believe me. It works.
W: I feel much better now. Thanks, Daniel.

questions.stem: Why does Daniel mention his performance in a play?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第11题对话。M: Sure. Do you remember that play I was in a few years ago? I knew my lines, but I was terrified to have to recite them in front of an audience.

questions.stem: What is Nancy going to do next week?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第11题对话。W: That's how I feel just thinking about the spelling competition next week.

questions.stem: What does Daniel offer to do for Nancy?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第11题对话。M: I'll help you get through this. I'll go to the school hall with you to practice. Then I'll teach you an exercise my baseball coach taught me.

questions.stem: What was Prof. Stone's grandfather afraid of?
questions.transcript:
【原文】W: Hello, ladies and gentlemen! Today, we have invited Prof. Stone to talk about the role of elderly people in our society. Welcome to our show, Prof. Stone.
M: To begin with, I'd like to tell a story from my own life. Several years ago, when my grandparents were well into their 80s, they were no longer able to care for themselves very well. My grandfather was afraid of leaving the only home they had known for the past 60 years. The idea of having to sell their home and move into a retirement home was an extremely painful experience for them. Indeed, old age for them, and many old Americans, can mean not only the possible failure of one's health, but the loss of identity and self-worth.
W: Yes, it's true. What do you have to say about the problem of old age?
M: Many experts have given talks here that have focused on the medical care, and the development of public services for senior citizens. Today, I'd like to focus my comments on the meaningful roles that elderly can play and should play in our society.

questions.stem: What does old age mean to many elderly Americans?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第15题对话。M: Indeed, old age for them, and many old Americans, can mean not only the possible failure of one's health, but the loss of identity and self-worth.

questions.stem: What will Prof. Stone talk about next concerning elderly people?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第15题对话。M: Today, I'd like to focus my comments on the meaningful roles that elderly can play and should play in our society.

questions.stem: What does the speaker's mother want her to be?
questions.transcript: 【原文】W: Talking about personal relationships. Well, I'd naturally think of my relationship with my mother. Whenever I need help, my mother is always there for me. She often tells me that I can be anyone I want, as long as I'm confident of myself. She sees my talent and pushes me to do the best I possibly can. As I was growing up, we were often on the move. I had to admit that moving so often made me feel lonely. But my mother did everything she could to help me feel happy. In fact, so much traveling was really a good thing because it made us close. I respect my mother so much as she never treats me as a child, but as an equal. She gives me the freedom to make mistakes and to learn from them all. Unlike friendships that can fade or break, I know I'll always be connected to my mother no matter what I face. She is not just a role model, but someone I love.

questions.stem: Why did the speaker feel lonely in her childhood?
questions.transcript: 【原文】同第18题独白。W: As I was growing up, we were often on the move. I had to admit that moving so often made me feel lonely.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly talk about?

options.text: A role model in her family.

questions.transcript: 【原文】同第18题独白。W: Talking about personal relationships. Well, I'd naturally think of my relationship with my mother.

sections.partTitle: 第一部分 阅读理解（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共15小题；每小题2分，满分30分）阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D四个选项中，选出最佳选项。

passages.label: A
passages.text:
A Take a view, the Landscape（风景）Photographer of the Year Award, was the idea of Charlie Waite, one of today's most respected landscape photographers. Each year, the high standard of entries has shown that the Awards are the perfect platform to showcase the very best photography of the British landscape. Take a view is a desirable annual competition for photographers from all corners of the UK and beyond.

Mike Shepherd(2011)
Skiddaw in Winter
Cumbria, England
It was an extremely cold winter's evening and freezing fog hung in the air. I climbed to the top of a small rise and realised that the mist was little more than a few feet deep, and though it was only a short climb, I found myself completely above it and looking at a wonderfully clear view of Skiddaw with the sun setting in the west. I used classical techniques, translated from my college days spent in the darkroom into Photoshop, to achieve the black—and—white image（图像）.

Timothy Smith(2014)
Macclesfield Forest
Cheshire, England
I was back in my home town of Macclesfield to take some winter images. Walking up a path through the forest towards Shutlingsloe, a local high point, I came across a small clearing and immediately noticed the dead yellow grasses set against the fresh snow. The small pine added to the interest and I placed it centrally to take the view from the foreground right through into the forest.

passages.label: B
passages.text:
Port Lympne Reserve, which runs a breeding (繁育) programme, has welcomed the arrival of a rare black rhino calf (犀牛幼崽). When the tiny creature arrived on January 31, she became the 40th black rhino to be born at the reserve. And officials at Port Lympne were delighted with the new arrival, especially as black rhinos are known for being difficult to breed in captivity (圈养).

Paul Beer, head of rhino section at Port Lympne, said: “Obviously we're all absolutely delighted to welcome another calf to our black rhino family. She's healthy, strong and already eager to play and explore. Her mother, Solio, is a first-time mum and she is doing a fantastic job. It's still a little too cold for them to go out into the open, but as soon as the weather warms up, I have no doubt that the little one will be out and about exploring and playing every day.”

The adorable female calf is the second black rhino born this year at the reserve, but it is too early to tell if the calves will make good candidates to be returned to protected areas of the wild. The first rhino to be born at Port Lympne arrived on January 5 to first-time mother Kisima and weighed about 32kg. His mother, grandmother and great grandmother were all born at the reserve and still live there.

According to the World Wildlife Fund, the global black rhino population has dropped as low as 5500, giving the rhinos a “critically endangered” status.

passages.label: C
passages.text:
When I was 9, we packed up our home in Los Angeles and arrived at Heathrow, London on a gray January morning. Everyone in the family settled quickly into the city except me. Without my beloved beaches and endless blue—sky days, I felt at a loss and out of place. Until I made a discovery.

Southbank, at an eastern bend in the Thames, is the center of British skateboarding, where the continuous crashing of skateboards left your head ringing. I loved it. I soon made friends with the local skaters. We spoke our own language. And my favorite: Safe. Safe meant cool. It meant hello. It meant don't worry about it. Once, when trying a certain trick on the beam（横杆）, I fell onto the stones, damaging a nerve in my hand, and Toby came over, helping me up: Safe, man. Safe. A few minutes later, when I landed the trick, my friends beat their boards loud, shouting: “Safe! Safe! Safe!” And that's what mattered—landing tricks, being a good skater.

When I was 15, my family moved to Washington. I tried skateboarding there, but the locals were far less welcoming. Within a couple of years, I'd given it up.

When I returned to London in 2004, I found myself wandering down to Southbank, spending hours there. I've traveled back several times since, most recently this past spring. The day was cold but clear: tourists and Londoners stopped to watch the skaters. Weaving（穿梭）among the kids who rushed by on their boards, I found my way to the beam. Then a rail—thin teenager, in a baggy white T—shirt, skidded（滑）up to the beam. He sat next to me. He seemed not to notice the man next to him. But soon I caught a few of his glances. “I was a local here 20 years ago,” I told him. Then, slowly, he began to nod his head. “Safe, man. Safe.”

“Yeah,” I said. “Safe.”

passages.label: D
passages.text:
Who is a genius? This question has greatly interested humankind for centuries.

Let's state clearly: Einstein was a genius. His face is almost the international symbol for genius. But we want to go beyond one man and explore the nature of genius itself. Why is it that some people are so much more intelligent or creative than the rest of us? And who are they?

In the sciences and arts, those praised as geniuses were most often white men, of European origin. Perhaps this is not a surprise. It's said that history is written by the victors, and those victors set the standards for admission to the genius club. When contributions were made by geniuses outside the club—women, or people of a different color or belief—they were unacknowledged and rejected by others.

A study recently published by Science found that as young as age six, girls are less likely than boys to say that members of their gender(性别)are “really, really smart.” Even worse, the study found that girls act on that belief: Around age six they start to avoid activities said to be for children who are “really, really smart.” Can our planet afford to have any great thinkers become discouraged and give up? It doesn't take a genius to know the answer: absolutely not.

Here's the good news. In a wired world with constant global communication, we're all positioned to see flashes of genius wherever they appear. And the more we look, the more we will see that social factors(因素)like gender, race, and class do not determine the appearance of genius. As a writer says, future geniuses come from those with “intelligence, creativity, perseverance(毅力), and simple good fortune, who are able to change the world.”

questions.stem: Who would most probably enter for Take a view?

explanation.question: 题干问谁最有可能报名参加 Take a view，需回到首段对赛事性质的界定。
explanation.evidence: Take a view, the Landscape(风景) Photographer of the Year Award, was the idea of Charlie Waite, one of today's most respected landscape photographers.
explanation.answer: B。该奖项是“年度风景摄影师奖”，参赛者自然是摄影师。

questions.stem: What do the works by Shepherd and Smith have in common?

options.text: They are in black and white.

explanation.question: 比较两位摄影师作品的共同点，需分别在两段自述中找时间/季节线索。
explanation.evidence: Shepherd：It was an extremely cold winter's evening…；Smith：I was back in my home town of Macclesfield to take some winter images.
explanation.answer: A。两幅作品都是冬季景象；黑白只有 Shepherd 一人，故 B 错。

questions.stem: Where can the text be found?

explanation.question: 根据全文体裁与内容判断刊载载体。
explanation.evidence: the Awards are the perfect platform to showcase the very best photography of the British landscape… Take a view is a desirable annual competition for photographers…
explanation.answer: C。介绍摄影比赛及获奖作品，最可能出现在艺术类杂志。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the breeding programme?

explanation.question: 评价该繁育计划，需抓“第40头”“祖孙三代都在此出生”等成效数据。
explanation.evidence: she became the 40th black rhino to be born at the reserve；His mother, grandmother and great grandmother were all born at the reserve and still live there.
explanation.answer: D。黑犀牛圈养繁育困难，却已成功繁育 40 头且多代存活，说明计划是成功的。

questions.stem: What does Paul Beer say about the new-born rhino?

options.text: She loves staying with her mother.

explanation.question: 定位 Paul Beer 的直接引语，看他如何描述新生犀牛。
explanation.evidence: She's healthy, strong and already eager to play and explore.
explanation.answer: C。健康、强壮即身体状况良好；不外出是因为天冷，不是不喜欢户外，故 B、D 错。

questions.stem: What similar experience do Solio and Kisima have?

options.text: They had their first born in January.
They were brought to the reserve young.

explanation.question: 对比两头母犀牛的经历，需把两处日期与“first-time mum”并读。
explanation.evidence: When the tiny creature arrived on January 31…（母亲 Solio 是 first-time mum）；The first rhino to be born at Port Lympne arrived on January 5 to first-time mother Kisima.
explanation.answer: A。两头母犀牛都是初次生产，且都在一月份分娩。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about Port Lympne Reserve?

options.text: The rhino section will be open to the public.
It aims to control the number of the animals.
It will continue to work with the World Wildlife Fund.
Some of its rhinos may be sent to the protected wild areas.

explanation.question: 根据保护区对幼崽未来去向的表述作合理推断。
explanation.evidence: it is too early to tell if the calves will make good candidates to be returned to protected areas of the wild
explanation.answer: D。“是否适合放归野生保护区尚难判断”暗示部分犀牛可能被送往野生保护区。

questions.stem: What can we learn about the author soon after he moved to London?

options.text: He had disagreements with his family.

explanation.question: 问刚搬到伦敦时作者的状态，定位首段的自我感受。
explanation.evidence: Everyone in the family settled quickly into the city except me. Without my beloved beaches and endless blue—sky days, I felt at a loss and out of place.
explanation.answer: A。失去心爱的沙滩与晴空，感到迷茫、格格不入，即失落沮丧。

questions.stem: What do the underlined words “Safe! Safe! Safe!” probably mean?

explanation.question: 画线处出现在作者成功完成动作、朋友敲板欢呼之时，需借后文点题句判断褒扬义。
explanation.evidence: when I landed the trick, my friends beat their boards loud, shouting: “Safe! Safe! Safe!” And that's what mattered—landing tricks, being a good skater.
explanation.answer: B。此处为称赞“干得漂亮”。

questions.stem: Why did the author like to spend time in Southbank when he returned to London?

explanation.question: 问重返伦敦后常去 Southbank 的原因，结合末段与少年的对话。
explanation.evidence: “I was a local here 20 years ago,” I told him. Then, slowly, he began to nod his head. “Safe, man. Safe.”
explanation.answer: D。作者是去重温少年时代的滑板记忆，而非重新练习技巧。

questions.stem: What message does the author seem to convey in the text?

options.text: Children should learn a second language.
Sport is necessary for children's health.
Children need a sense of belonging.
Seeing the world is a must for children.

explanation.question: 概括作者借自身经历要传达的观点。
explanation.evidence: 在伦敦因滑板圈接纳而融入；在华盛顿因“the locals were far less welcoming”而放弃；多年后重返仍在寻找那份熟悉感。
explanation.answer: C。归属感对孩子至关重要。

questions.stem: What does the author think of victors' standards for joining the genius club?

explanation.question: 问作者如何评价“胜利者”设定的天才俱乐部准入标准。
explanation.evidence: those victors set the standards for admission to the genius club. When contributions were made by geniuses outside the club—women, or people of a different color or belief—they were unacknowledged and rejected by others.
explanation.answer: A。女性与不同肤色、信仰者的贡献得不到承认，说明标准不公平。

questions.stem: What can we infer about girls from the study in Science?

options.text: They look up to great thinkers.
They see gender differences earlier than boys.
They are likely to be influenced by social beliefs.

explanation.question: 根据 Science 研究结论推断女孩受到的影响。
explanation.evidence: Even worse, the study found that girls act on that belief: Around age six they start to avoid activities said to be for children who are “really, really smart.”
explanation.answer: D。女孩按社会观念行事，说明易受社会信念影响。

questions.stem: Why are more geniuses known to the public?

explanation.question: 问更多天才为公众所知的原因，定位末段首句。
explanation.evidence: In a wired world with constant global communication, we're all positioned to see flashes of genius wherever they appear.
explanation.answer: A。全球通讯的进步让人们随时随地看到天才的闪现。

questions.stem: What is the best title for the text?

explanation.question: 由首段设问与末段引语归纳全文中心。
explanation.evidence: Who is a genius?…future geniuses come from those with “intelligence, creativity, perseverance, and simple good fortune, who are able to change the world.”
explanation.answer: B。文章论证天才并非只有一种模样，形式多样。

sections.partTitle: 第一部分 阅读理解（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共5小题；每小题2分，满分10分）根据短文内容，从短文后的选项中选出能填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

passages.label: Swap, Don't shop!
passages.text:
You keep hearing about recycling, right? But it doesn't end with bottles, cans, and paper. Clothing takes a huge amount of natural resources（资源）to make, and buying loads of new clothing（or throwing out old clothing）is not healthy for the environment. So what to do with all those perfectly-good-but-you're-maybe-a-little-sick-of-them clothes piled on your bedroom floor? ___36___. It's the best way to get rid of your used clothes, score clothes from your friends, and have a party all at the same time.

A successful swap depends on the selection of clothes, the organization of the event, and, obviously, how much fun is had. It's really easy to do! Here are a few pointers.

● Invite 5—10 people so you have a nice selection. ___37___ , and there may not be enough things to choose from; more than that, and it becomes uncontrollable.

● ___38___. They should also prepare plenty of reusable bags to carry their "new" clothes home.

● Put different types of clothing on different surfaces in the room. ___39___. Place a few mirrors around your room so people can see how things look when they try them on. One of the ground rules of the swap should be that everyone must try on the clothes before they take them—things always look different when you put them on.

● Set a starting time. Maybe you say “go,” or turn on a certain song, or whatever. ___40___. And don't forget to put out some cookies and fruits. Remember, it's a party!

A. Less people than that
B. Hold a clothing swap
C. If two people are competing
D. Just keep music playing throughout
E. Donate whatever clothes are left over
F. Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
G. Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

pool.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

questions.stem: 第36空

options.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

explanation.question: 上文提出“堆在地板上的旧衣服怎么办”的问题，下文说“这是处理旧衣服、从朋友那里换衣服并同时开派对的最好方法”，空处需给出这个“方法”。
explanation.evidence: So what to do with all those…clothes piled on your bedroom floor? ___36___. It's the best way to get rid of your used clothes…
explanation.answer: B。“举办一次换衣活动”正是下文 It 所指的方法。

questions.stem: 第37空

options.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

explanation.question: 上文建议邀请 5—10 人，下文用 more than that 说人多的弊端，空处应是人少的相反假设。
explanation.evidence: Invite 5—10 people…___37___, and there may not be enough things to choose from; more than that, and it becomes uncontrollable.
explanation.answer: A。与 more than that 形成“人少 / 人多”对照。

questions.stem: 第38空

options.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

explanation.summary: 段首主题句（代词与 also 提示）
explanation.question: 下文 They should also prepare…bags 中的 They 需在空处找到指代对象，also 表明空处也是对参与者的要求。
explanation.evidence: ___38___. They should also prepare plenty of reusable bags to carry their "new" clothes home.
explanation.answer: G。Tell everyone… 中的 everyone 即下文的 They，bring 与 carry 呼应。

questions.stem: 第39空

options.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

explanation.question: 上文讲把不同类型衣服分区摆放，下文讲放镜子，空处仍应是房间内的具体做法。
explanation.evidence: Put different types of clothing on different surfaces in the room. ___39___. Place a few mirrors around your room…
explanation.answer: F。让每个人把衣服放到对应位置，与“分类摆放”一致。

questions.stem: 第40空

options.text: Donate whatever clothes are left over
Have everyone put their clothes in the right spots
Tell everyone to bring clean clothes in good condition

explanation.question: 上文提到用歌曲宣布开始，下文说别忘了点心水果“这是个派对”，空处应延续派对氛围的做法。
explanation.evidence: Maybe you say “go,” or turn on a certain song, or whatever. ___40___. And don't forget to put out some cookies and fruits. Remember, it's a party!
explanation.answer: D。全程放着音乐，与前文 turn on a certain song 一致。

sections.partTitle: 第二部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共20小题；每小题1.5分，满分30分）阅读下面短文，从短文后各题所给的A、B、C和D四个选项中，选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。

passages.label: 完形填空
passages.text:
It's the seaside birds that deserve at least part of the blame for getting Nick Burchill blacklisted at the Fairmont Empress Hotel in Victoria, Canada.

Burchill was ___41___ at the hotel on business and planning to ___42___ some friends in the area. They had asked him to ___43___ some pepperoni (辣香肠) from back east. So he ___44___ a suitcase full of pepperoni. As he was ___45___ that it would be too warm, he ___46___ it out on the table near an open window. He thought his pepperoni was ___47___ and well chilled (冷却) and he ___48___ .

That's when things went ___49___ . “I remember walking down the long ___50___ and opening the door to my room to find an entire flock of seagulls,” Burchill said in a recent letter of ___51___ to the 4-star hotel. "The seagulls immediately went ___52___ . They rushed to the window, 30 or 40 birds all trying to ___53___ at the same time, and pepperoni—everywhere. The curtains were falling down, the lamps were falling down. It was a real ___54___ .

Older and wiser now, Burchill chalked up the incident to youthful indiscretion (莽撞).

“I have ___55___ and I admit responsibility of my ___56___ ,” he said in the letter. “I come to you, ___57___ , to apologize for the damage I had ___58___ caused and to ask you to ___59___ my lifetime ban from the hotel.”

His letter ___60___ . Banned from the hotel since 2001, Burchill is now welcome to come back, the Fairmont said.

questions.stem: 第41空

explanation.question: 句意：Burchill 出差期间正在酒店收拾行李，准备去拜访当地的一些朋友。A. 研究；B. 停留；C. 看；D. 收拾（行李）。
explanation.evidence: Burchill was ___41___ at the hotel on business and planning to ___42___ some friends in the area.
explanation.answer: D。下文他“装了满满一箱香肠”，可见此刻在收拾行李。

questions.stem: 第42空

explanation.question: A. 拜访；B. 帮助；C. 跟随；D. 制作。
explanation.evidence: They had asked him to ___43___ some pepperoni from back east.
explanation.answer: A。朋友托他带东西，说明他要去拜访这些朋友。

questions.stem: 第43空

explanation.question: A. 卖；B. 有；C. 带来；D. 品尝。
explanation.evidence: So he ___44___ a suitcase full of pepperoni.
explanation.answer: C。朋友让他从东部带些辣香肠过来。

questions.stem: 第44空

explanation.question: A. 装满；B. 锁上；C. 抛弃；D. 丢失。
explanation.evidence: a suitcase full of pepperoni；下文 and pepperoni—everywhere.
explanation.answer: A。他装了满满一箱辣香肠。

questions.stem: 第45空

explanation.question: A. 惊讶的；B. 高兴的；C. 兴奋的；D. 担心的。
explanation.evidence: As he was ___45___ that it would be too warm, he ___46___ it out on the table near an open window.
explanation.answer: D。担心香肠太热，才把它摊在开着的窗户旁。

questions.stem: 第46空

explanation.question: A. 挖；B. 清除；C. 切；D. 放置（lay out 摊开摆放）。
explanation.evidence: he ___46___ it out on the table near an open window
explanation.answer: D。lay it out on the table 把它摊放在桌上。

questions.stem: 第47空

explanation.question: A. 美味的；B. 安全的；C. 柔软的；D. 准备好的。
explanation.evidence: He thought his pepperoni was ___47___ and well chilled and he ___48___ .
explanation.answer: B。他以为香肠很安全、冷却良好，于是离开了。

questions.stem: 第48空

explanation.question: A. 离开；B. 点头；C. 等待；D. 后悔。
explanation.evidence: I remember walking down the long ___50___ and opening the door to my room…
explanation.answer: A。后文他“走过走廊、开门回房”，说明先前离开了。

questions.stem: 第49空

explanation.question: A. 远的；B. 有趣的；C. 出问题的；D. 盲目的。
explanation.evidence: The curtains were falling down, the lamps were falling down. It was a real ___54___ .
explanation.answer: C。things went wrong 事情就在此时出了问题。

questions.stem: 第50空

explanation.question: A. 海滩；B. 私人车道；C. 走廊/大厅；D. 桌子。
explanation.evidence: walking down the long ___50___ and opening the door to my room
explanation.answer: C。走过长长的走廊后开房门，符合酒店场景。

questions.stem: 第51空

explanation.question: A. 申请；B. 道歉；C. 要求；D. 邀请。
explanation.evidence: to apologize for the damage I had ___58___ caused and to ask you to ___59___ my lifetime ban
explanation.answer: B。信中明确 apologize，故为道歉信。

questions.stem: 第52空

explanation.question: A. 饥饿的；B. 死的；C. 失踪的；D. 疯狂的。
explanation.evidence: They rushed to the window, 30 or 40 birds all trying to ___53___ at the same time
explanation.answer: D。海鸥被突然回来的人惊到，立刻发起狂来。

questions.stem: 第53空

explanation.question: A. 醒来；B. 出去；C. 起飞；D. 闯入。
explanation.evidence: They rushed to the window, 30 or 40 birds all trying to ___53___ at the same time
explanation.answer: B。群鸟冲向窗口，都想同时逃出去。

questions.stem: 第54空

explanation.question: A. 一团糟；B. 谜；C. 打架；D. 挑战。
explanation.evidence: The curtains were falling down, the lamps were falling down.
explanation.answer: A。窗帘、台灯纷纷倒下，现场一片混乱。

questions.stem: 第55空

explanation.question: A. 恢复；B. 退休；C. 逃跑；D. 成熟。
explanation.evidence: Older and wiser now…“I have ___55___ and I admit responsibility of my ___56___ .”
explanation.answer: D。承接 Older and wiser，他表示自己已经成熟。

questions.stem: 第56空

explanation.question: A. 苦难；B. 计划；C. 疯狂；D. 行为。
explanation.evidence: I admit responsibility of my ___56___ … to apologize for the damage I had ___58___ caused
explanation.answer: D。他承认要为自己的行为负责。

questions.stem: 第57空

explanation.question: A. 手插口袋；B. 目中无人；C. 恭恭敬敬地；D. 脚踏实地。
explanation.evidence: I come to you, ___57___ , to apologize for the damage…
explanation.answer: C。hat in hand 表示毕恭毕敬，与道歉语境相符。

questions.stem: 第58空

explanation.question: A. 间接地；B. 故意地；C. 谨慎地；D. 秘密地。
explanation.evidence: 香肠招来海鸥，海鸥逃跑时弄坏了房间物品——损失并非他直接造成。
explanation.answer: A。损害是他间接造成的。

questions.stem: 第59空

explanation.question: A. 取代；B. 记得；C. 重新考虑；D. 更新。
explanation.evidence: to ask you to ___59___ my lifetime ban from the hotel；Burchill is now welcome to come back
explanation.answer: C。他请求酒店重新考虑终身禁入的决定。

questions.stem: 第60空

explanation.question: A. 到达；B. 起作用；C. 结束；D. 消失。
explanation.evidence: Banned from the hotel since 2001, Burchill is now welcome to come back, the Fairmont said.
explanation.answer: B。禁令被解除，说明他的信起了作用。

sections.partTitle: 第二部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共10小题；每小题1.5分，满分15分）阅读下面短文，在空白处填入1个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

passages.label: 语法填空
passages.text:
The Xi'an City Wall is the most complete city wall that has survived China's long history. It ___61___ (build) originally to protect the city ___62___ the Tang dynasty and has now been completely restored (修复). It is possible ___63___ (walk) or bike the entire 14 kilometers.

We accessed the wall through the South Gate. The wall is 12 meters high and from here you can see streams of people moving inside and outside the City Wall.

After ___64___ (spend) some time looking at all the defensive equipment at the wall, we decided it was time for some action and what ___65___ (good) than to ride on a piece of history!

We ___66___ (hire) our bikes from the rental place at the South Gate. My bike was old and shaky ___67___ did the job. It took us about 3 hours to go all ___68___ way around the Xi'an City Wall. Supposedly you can do it in two hours, but we stopped at the different gates and ___69___ (watchtower) to take pictures or just to watch the local people going about their ___70___ (day) routines.

questions.stem: 第61空 It ___61___ (build) originally to protect the city…

explanation.summary: 被动语态 + 一般过去时
explanation.question: 空处作谓语，build 与主语 It（城墙）是被动关系，时间状语 the Tang dynasty 提示一般过去时，主语第三人称单数。
explanation.evidence: It ___61___ (build) originally to protect the city ___62___ the Tang dynasty
explanation.answer: was built

questions.stem: 第62空 to protect the city ___62___ the Tang dynasty

explanation.question: 表示“在某个朝代”，用介词 in。
explanation.evidence: to protect the city ___62___ the Tang dynasty
explanation.answer: in

questions.stem: 第63空 It is possible ___63___ (walk) or bike the entire 14 kilometers.

explanation.summary: 动词不定式作真正主语
explanation.question: 句型 It is + adj. + to do sth.，it 为形式主语。
explanation.evidence: It is possible ___63___ (walk) or bike the entire 14 kilometers.
explanation.answer: to walk

questions.stem: 第64空 After ___64___ (spend) some time looking at…

explanation.question: After 在此为介词，其后动词用动名词形式。
explanation.evidence: After ___64___ (spend) some time looking at all the defensive equipment
explanation.answer: spending

questions.stem: 第65空 what ___65___ (good) than to ride on a piece of history!

explanation.question: 后有比较连词 than，需用 good 的比较级。
explanation.evidence: what ___65___ (good) than to ride on a piece of history!
explanation.answer: better

questions.stem: 第66空 We ___66___ (hire) our bikes from the rental place…

explanation.question: 空处作谓语，全文叙述过去经历，用一般过去时。
explanation.evidence: We ___66___ (hire) our bikes from the rental place at the South Gate.
explanation.answer: hired

questions.stem: 第67空 My bike was old and shaky ___67___ did the job.

explanation.question: 前后为“又旧又晃”与“但还能用”的转折关系。
explanation.evidence: My bike was old and shaky ___67___ did the job.
explanation.answer: but

questions.stem: 第68空 It took us about 3 hours to go all ___68___ way around…

explanation.question: all the way 意为“一路；完全地”。
explanation.evidence: to go all ___68___ way around the Xi'an City Wall
explanation.answer: the

questions.stem: 第69空 we stopped at the different gates and ___69___ (watchtower)

explanation.question: 受前面 different 制约，watchtower 表复数概念。
explanation.evidence: we stopped at the different gates and ___69___ (watchtower) to take pictures
explanation.answer: watchtowers

questions.stem: 第70空 going about their ___70___ (day) routines

explanation.question: 修饰名词 routines 需用形容词形式。
explanation.evidence: to watch the local people going about their ___70___ (day) routines
explanation.answer: daily

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节 短文改错（共10小题；每小题1分，满分10分）

questions.stem: 假定英语课上老师要求同桌之间交换修改作业，请你修改你同桌写的以下作文。文中共有10处语言错误，每句中最多有两处。每处错误仅涉及一个单词的增加、删除或修改。
questions.material:
增加：在缺词处加一个漏字符号（∧），并在其下面写出该加的词。
删除：把多余的词用斜线（\）划掉。
修改：在错的词下划一横线，并在该词下面写出修改后的词。
注意：1. 每处错误及其修改均仅限一词；
2. 只允许修改10处，多者（从第11处起）不计分。

Last week our teacher asked us to fill in a questionnaire. One of the questions are: Who will you go in times of trouble? Here are the results. Many students say they will talk to their friend or classmates because they're of the same age and can understand each other. Some will turn out to their parents or teachers for help. Only a little choose to deal with the problems on our own. Their answers also show that they dislike talk to others. They kept very much to themselves. In my opinion, where in trouble, we should seek help from those we trust mostly.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. 把‘are’改为‘is’
2. 在‘go’后加上‘to’
3. 把‘friend’改为‘friends’
4. 删去‘turn 后的 out’
5. 把‘little’改为‘few’
6. 把‘our’改为‘their’
7. 把‘talk’改为‘talking’
8. 把‘kept’改为‘keep’
9. 把‘where’改为‘when/whenever’
10. 把‘mostly’改为‘most’

explanation.summary: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍了关于学生遇到问题后解决方式的问卷调查结果。

points.note: one of the + 复数名词作主语时为单数含义，且陈述客观事实用一般现在时。
go to sb.“求助于某人”，相当于 turn to sb. for help。
与 their 及并列的 classmates 一致，用复数。
turn to sb. for help 中无 out。
指代可数名词 students，用 a few；a little 指代不可数名词。
on one's own 中的物主代词应与主语（学生们）一致。
dislike doing sth. 不喜欢做某事。
全文陈述调查结论用一般现在时。
此处表“当/无论何时我们遇到麻烦”，用时间状语从句连词。
此处表程度“最信任的”，用 most；mostly 意为“大多数情况下”。

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节 书面表达（满分25分）

questions.stem:
假定你是李华。你校计划举办介绍中国传统文化的主题班会，并在英文网站展示。请你写一封邮件给外国朋友Chris，向他了解哪些中国传统文化更吸引外国友人。邮件内容包括：
1. 阐明写信事由；
2. 征求建议；
3. 表示感谢。
注意：
1. 词数100左右；
2. 可以适当增加细节，以使行文连贯。
questions.modelAnswer:
Dear Chris,

Word came that our school is going to hold a class meeting whose topic is related to Chinese traditional customs. Because this activity will be presented on the English website, I sincerely want you to offer me some advice.

As far as we know, there is a huge cultural difference between China and the western countries. In order to get more clicks, you'd better tell me which Chinese culture you westerners prefer. What's more, if I want to decorate my website with some Chinese elements, what should I do? Knowing you are interested in China, I do believe you can help me solve these puzzles.

If possible, you can reply to me as soon as possible. I will take your advice into consideration. I really appreciate your help.

Yours,
Li Hua

explanation.summary: 应用文（邮件）· 写作要点
explanation.question: 本文要求写一封询问建议的邮件，需覆盖三个要点：说明写信缘由（班会介绍中国传统文化并在英文网站展示）、征求建议（哪些中国传统文化更吸引外国友人）、表示感谢。
explanation.evidence: 时态以一般现在时和一般将来时为主，人称为第一人称；注意邮件格式（称呼、正文分段、结尾署名）。
explanation.answer: 参考范文见上方“参考答案”。评分关注要点完整、语言准确、行文连贯与词汇句式的丰富度。
